data.name: Filemon
data.gender_notes: Filemon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Filemon means 'Soldier of Philo'. This name has biblical roots as it is mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in the book of Philemon. It is believed that Filemon was a wealthy man who had a runaway slave named Onesimus. After Onesimus encountered Paul and was converted to Christianity, Paul wrote a letter to Filemon urging him to forgive Onesimus and take him back.
data.etymology: Filemon belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier of Philo.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Filemon total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_latin.name: Philemon
in_latin.long_meaning: Philemon is a Latinized form of the Greek name Φιλήμων, meaning beloved and friendly. In the early Christian Church, Philemon was a slave who received mercy from St. Paul.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Filemon originates from the Greek name Φιλήμων, meaning friendly, lovable, and kind. In the New Testament, Philemon was a Christian slave owner who showed mercy and kindness, reflecting the spiritual significance of forgiveness and love.
